title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: AUB Connected Persons
tiers.description: Directors, officers, employees and contractors of the Company. The policy applies to all of them, but only the insider trading prohibition (7.4) and the general obligation to comply bite at this level; Blackout Periods, clearance and the specified prohibitions in 7.8 and 7.9 are expressed to apply only to Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors, officers and members of the Group Executive, plus any employee, contractor or closely connected person of an employee or contractor (including of Tysers) designated by the CEO or CFO from time to time, on a register maintained by the Company Secretary. Blackout Periods, prior written clearance, the margin lending approval and the short term dealing and short selling bans apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Key management personnel (including the Directors) as disclosed in the Company's Annual Report. Distinguished only for clearance: KMP other than the Chair, and the Chief Legal and Risk Officer, are cleared by the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished only for clearance, which must come from the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company. Within Designated Persons and KMP for trading purposes, and separately obliged to notify the Company of all changes in their notifiable interests for ASX Listing Rule 3.19A and s205G purposes.

tiers.name: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan
tiers.description: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan, expressly stated to include Designated Persons. This is the only tier to which the hedging prohibition in 7.7 is addressed.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse, de-facto spouse, parent or child (or a spouse or de-facto spouse of that parent or child); an entity controlled by one or more of those persons; any entity (including trusts, companies and nominees) or person that the AUB Connected Person controls or may be expected to control or influence; and any person acting or proposing to act in concert in relation to the Company's affairs. AUB Connected Persons must take reasonable steps to ensure Associates comply.

definitions.hedging_definition: a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock

windows.end_anchor: the day after the Company releases its half-year results to the ASX
the day after the Company releases its full-year results to the ASX

windows.end_anchor: the date of the Annual General Meeting (inclusive)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine 'any additional periods' as Blackout Periods from time to time (7.1(d)). The policy is silent on whether such periods are announced or kept confidential, and on who lifts them.

rules.detail: There is no standalone derivatives rule. 'Securities' is defined to include derivatives, structured financial products, swaps and warrants with no venue limitation, and 'Deal' includes purchasing or selling or entering into an agreement to do so. Buying a put or writing a call over Company shares is therefore a Dealing in Company Securities: permitted only outside Blackout Periods, with prior written clearance, and with no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Securities includes shares, options, rights, debentures, or other securities or derivatives including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, or warrant.

rules.detail: For an AUB Connected Person who is not a Designated Person, no Blackout Period or clearance requirement is imposed; only the absolute insider trading prohibition and (if a plan participant) the 7.7 hedging ban apply.
rules.evidence: Additional restrictions in this policy apply to Designated Persons, including requirements relating to Blackout Periods, clearance to Deal and other specified prohibitions.

rules.tier: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan
rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route, on any transaction limiting the economic risk of unvested Company Securities. A collar over unvested plan securities is squarely prohibited.
rules.evidence: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan (which includes Designated Persons) are prohibited from entering into a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock.

rules.tier: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan
rules.detail: The ban extends past vesting to vested securities that remain subject to a transfer restriction such as a holding lock, so shares under a disposal restriction period cannot be collared even though they have vested.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock.

rules.detail: The 7.7 prohibition is limited by its terms to unvested securities and to vested securities still subject to a transfer restriction. Hedging vested, unrestricted shares (whether plan-sourced or bought on market) is not prohibited; it is caught only as a Dealing in derivative Securities requiring prior written clearance outside a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not Deal in Company Securities at any time (including outside a Blackout Period) without prior written clearance

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collar-plus-loan structures are not named. A prepaid forward or an agreement to sell is an 'agreement to do' a sale and so a Dealing requiring prior written clearance; the derivative legs are themselves Securities. Any loan leg secured on the shares must additionally be run past 7.8.
rules.evidence: Deal includes directly or indirectly applying for, subscribing for, purchasing or selling or entering into an agreement to do any of those things

rules.detail: Flat prohibition on short selling Company Securities, with no clearance route. Written calls settled against shares the person owns are not short sales, but any leg that leaves the person net short would breach.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term Dealing or short selling in Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned anywhere in the policy and are not within the definition of Deal, which is confined to applying for, subscribing for, purchasing, selling and agreements to do those things.

CFDs and spread bets are expressly listed within the definition of Securities, so dealing in one is a Dealing requiring prior written clearance outside a Blackout Period. A short CFD would additionally breach the short selling ban and a CFD closed out inside 12 months the short term dealing ban.
rules.evidence: other securities or derivatives including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, or warrant.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted but not by right: prior approval is required, and it must come from the Chair of the Board (or the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee in their absence) rather than the ordinary clearance officer. Approval is expressly required for entering the arrangement, for transferring shares into an existing margin loan account, and for selling shares to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained prior to a Designated Person entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge is not itself within the definition of Deal and no general encumbrance rule exists. The only encumbrance regime is 7.8, and the policy directs anyone uncertain whether an arrangement is a margin lending arrangement to consult the Chief Legal and Risk Officer, so a lender's security over Company Securities should be treated as requiring Chair approval.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons should consult with the Company's Chief Legal and Risk Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: There is no blanket ban on secured financing. The policy addresses only 'margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities', which is not defined; a bank loan secured on collared shares is on its face such an arrangement, and in any event the uncertainty clause routes it to the Chief Legal and Risk Officer and then to Chair approval. Nothing prohibits the financing outright.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained prior to a Designated Person entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Short term Dealing is prohibited outright, with a 12 month intention-based benchmark running both ways (buy with a view to resale, or sell with a view to repurchase). The only carve-out is an immediate sale of securities acquired on conversion of another security, such as exercise of a share right.
rules.evidence: In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to their resale within a 12 month period, or the sale of Company Securities with a view to their repurchase within a 12 month period, will be considered to be a Dealing of a 'short term' nature.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within one business day of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: the Chair of the Board requires clearance from the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within one business day of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: Key Management Personnel (excluding the Chair) and the Chief Legal and Risk Officer require clearance from the Chair of the Board

clearance.approver: Chief Legal and Risk Officer (all Designated Persons other than the Chair, KMP and the CLRO). Margin lending approvals and exceptional-circumstances approvals must instead come from the Chair of the Board, or the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee in the Chair's absence.
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within one business day of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: Any clearance granted: (d) will be valid for a period of 7 calendar days from the date of approval; and (e) may be withdrawn at any time prior to the Dealing occurring. Any Dealing must occur within the period of the approval.
Additional restrictions in this policy apply to Designated Persons, including requirements relating to Blackout Periods, clearance to Deal and other specified prohibitions.

clearance.post_trade_to: the Company, for ASX Listing Rule 3.19A and section 250G purposes
clearance.post_trade_deadline: in time for the Company to meet its ASX Listing Rule notification obligations
clearance.evidence: Directors must give the Company notice of all changes in their notifiable interests (as defined in the ASX Listing Rules) so as to ensure compliance with the notification obligations of the Company and its Directors under ASX Listing Rule 3.19A and section 250G of the Corporations Act.

short_term.basis: from acquisition, and in reverse from disposal
carve_outs: The sale of Company Securities immediately after they have been acquired through the conversion of another security (e.g. exercise of a share right)
short_term.evidence: In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to their resale within a 12 month period, or the sale of Company Securities with a view to their repurchase within a 12 month period, will be considered to be a Dealing of a 'short term' nature.

exceptions.evidence: A Designated Person may be permitted to Deal in Company Securities during a Blackout Period where: (a) exceptional circumstances exist; and (b) prior written clearance has been obtained ... Exceptional circumstances may include ... severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or, in their absence, the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee)
exceptions.evidence: a requirement to comply with a court order or other legal or regulatory obligation

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or, in their absence, the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee)
exceptions.evidence: any other circumstance considered exceptional by the approver. The Designated Person must demonstrate that the proposed Dealing is the only reasonable course of action available.

transfer Company Securities between the Designated Person and an Associate of the Designated Person (including a transfer into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary), provided prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with paragraph 7.3

deal in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

undertake to accept, or accept a takeover offer

external_documents: Register of designated employees, contractors and closely connected persons maintained by the Company Secretary (7.1 / definition of Designated Person)
Company employee incentive plan rules (referred to in 7.6(f)-(g) and 7.7 but not reproduced)
exemption_authority: The Chair of the Board, or in the Chair's absence the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee, may permit Dealing during a Blackout Period in exceptional circumstances (7.5) and must approve margin lending arrangements (7.8). The Board may add Blackout Periods (7.1(d)) and approves the policy. The CEO or CFO designate additional Designated Persons. There is no exemption from the hedging prohibition in 7.7 or the short selling and short term dealing prohibitions in 7.9.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested and locked securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Participants in a Company employee incentive plan (which includes Designated Persons) are prohibited from entering into a transaction that limits the economic risk of unvested Company Securities or vested Company Securities that are subject to a restriction on transfer, such as a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban stops at vesting and release of the holding lock, so a collar over vested, unrestricted shares is not caught by it and remains available subject to clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval must be obtained prior to a Designated Person entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities. Such Dealings would cover: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Company Securities; (b) transferring Company Securities into an existing margin loan account; and (c) selling Company Securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban all secured financing, AUB only requires Chair approval, so the loan leg of a funded collar is permissible if the Chair approves it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons should consult with the Company's Chief Legal and Risk Officer if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on collared shares should be put to the Chief Legal and Risk Officer up front, because if it is classified as margin lending the approval must come from the Chair rather than the ordinary clearance officer.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin call sale is a controlled dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Such Dealings would cover ... selling Company Securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A forced sale or enforcement by the financier is treated as the executive's own Dealing needing prior Chair approval, so a collar loan must not permit the bank to sell shares during a Blackout Period without that approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term Dealing or short selling in Company Securities. In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to their resale within a 12 month period, or the sale of Company Securities with a view to their repurchase within a 12 month period, will be considered to be a Dealing of a 'short term' nature.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar tenor of less than 12 months, or one with early unwind or roll features, risks being characterised as short term Dealing, so the structure should be written for at least 12 months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any clearance granted: (d) will be valid for a period of 7 calendar days from the date of approval; and (e) may be withdrawn at any time prior to the Dealing occurring. Any Dealing must occur within the period of the approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar and the secured loan must all complete within 7 calendar days of clearance, and the clearance can be pulled at any point before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Following any Dealing, the Designated Person must notify the Company Secretary within one business day.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into the collar, and any later unwind, roll or settlement, must be reported to the Company Secretary within one business day, and for Directors it will also feed the Appendix 3Y notifiable interest disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities includes shares, options, rights, debentures, or other securities or derivatives including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, or warrant.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so the OTC put and call written with a bank are themselves Company Securities and each leg is a Dealing subject to clearance and Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associate means ... an entity (including without limitation trusts, companies and nominees) and/or person that the AUB Connected Person controls or may be expected to control or influence.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust, company or nominee does not avoid the policy; the AUB Connected Person must take reasonable steps to ensure the Associate complies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person may be permitted to Deal in Company Securities during a Blackout Period where: (a) exceptional circumstances exist ... The Designated Person must demonstrate that the proposed Dealing is the only reasonable course of action available.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is a hardship and legal-obligation escape hatch approved by the Chair, but the 'only reasonable course of action' test means it will rarely support a discretionary collar entry or unwind inside a Blackout Period.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is unusually permissive: there is no blanket prohibition on hedging vested shares and no ban on secured financing. Over vested Company Securities that are no longer subject to a holding lock or other transfer restriction, a Designated Person may buy a put and write a call, since both legs are 'Securities' and each is a Dealing requiring only prior written clearance (Chair of the Board for KMP, the Chair of the Board Audit & Risk Committee for the Chair, the Chief Legal and Risk Officer for others), granted outside the 15 December, 15 June and pre-AGM Blackout Periods, valid for 7 calendar days, revocable before execution, and notified to the Company Secretary within one business day. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is not prohibited but should be treated as a margin lending arrangement, which requires separate prior approval from the Chair of the Board and, importantly, means any enforcement sale by the bank also needs prior Chair approval and cannot simply run during a Blackout Period. The structure must not extend to unvested plan securities or vested securities still subject to a holding lock, where hedging is absolutely prohibited with no exemption, and must not leave the executive net short. Tenor should exceed 12 months so the arrangement is not characterised as short term Dealing under section 7.9.
